solves: Gives the person a box with its own text, to check independent options or to turn one option on or off, and sends the choice with the form.
use_when: When the person can check more than one option, each independent.
For a single option, which the person turns on or off.
Indeterminate only on the item that summarizes a group checked in part: it is not an answer from the person.
The box alone only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell, always with label.
do_not_use_when: When the options exclude each other: use nph-radio.
Around it, an nph-field only to give it a name: the box already brings its own text.
To mix checkbox and radio in the same group.
To put a link in the text, such as the terms of use: the link stays outside the piece.
To paint the box or the mark by hand: the piece takes its colors from tokens.

checked.constraint: The current state, the Figma marcado true. It does not reflect: the checked attribute is the default state, the one a form reset goes back to. Once the person toggles the piece or code sets checked, the piece is dirty and the attribute no longer moves the current state, as on the native checkbox. Setting it from code fires no event.

indeterminate.constraint: A group checked only in part, the Figma marcado indeterminado. The box shows the minus mark whatever checked is. A click of the person clears it and toggles checked. It does not change what the form submits. Setting it from code fires no event.

text.constraint: The plain text next to the box, already localized by the consuming application: the name of the control. No link and no rich content inside it. It wraps, with the box at the top. Without text, the piece is only the box, at 24 by 24, and requires label.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the box alone; it becomes the aria-label of the inner checkbox. Without text and without label, the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development. With text, it is not used.

invalid.constraint: The error state of the Figma. The box border becomes status/error, checked or not, and the inner checkbox takes aria-invalid. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the border by it. The error sentence stays outside the piece. disabled wins over it.

disabled.constraint: The Figma state disabled. The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, text included; it leaves the Tab order, does not toggle, fires nothing and is not submitted. It is the disabled attribute of the host, set at once, so the host matches the disabled pseudo-class. A disabled fieldset has the same effect.

name.constraint: The name of the entry in the form data. It is the name attribute of the host: the form reads the attribute, so the property writes it.

value.constraint: What a checked piece submits under name. It is the value attribute of the host, on when the attribute is absent, as on the native checkbox.

checked.choose_when: Unchecked for an option that is off; checked for an option that is on; indeterminate only on the item that summarizes a group checked in part.

content.choose_when: With text in every case where the name must be visible. The box alone only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell; it takes label.
do_not_combine_with: the box alone without label: the screen reader would announce only checkbox.

unchecked.token: color/background for the fill and color/input for the border
unchecked.changes_for_user: An empty box, with the text next to it.

checked.token: color/primary for the fill and color/primary-foreground for the check mark; the border stays color/input
checked.changes_for_user: The box is filled and shows the check mark.

indeterminate.token: color/primary for the fill and color/primary-foreground for the minus mark
indeterminate.changes_for_user: The box is filled and shows the minus mark: the group is checked only in part.

hover.token: color/input-hover for the border; a checked or indeterminate box also takes state/hover-opacity
hover.changes_for_user: The whole piece responds, text included: the border gets one step darker.

focus.token: focus/border for the box border and a focus/halo band of focus/ring-width, radius focus/radius-inner; with error, status/error and focus/halo-error
focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, the box border changes color and a halo fills the 24 by 24 touch area, without changing the size.

invalid.changes_for_user: The box border becomes status/error, checked or not; the error sentence stays outside the piece.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole piece loses opacity, leaves the Tab order, stops responding and is not submitted.

business_rules: Only a click on the box or on the text, or Space, by the person toggles the piece; Enter does not. The native input event crosses the shadow root and the host fires change, which bubbles and is not composed. Setting checked or indeterminate from code fires nothing.

The checked attribute is the default state and the property is the current state, with the dirty flag of the native checkbox. A form reset goes back to the attribute, clears indeterminate and fires nothing.
A checked piece submits name=value with the form; unchecked, nothing. indeterminate does not change what is submitted. A disabled piece, also inside a disabled fieldset, submits nothing.
There is no required and no constraint validation: invalid never blocks the submission.
disabled wins over invalid: a disabled piece draws no error border and has no aria-invalid. It is not an error case.
Inside nph-field, the piece is an option of a group (nphFieldRole option): the field names and describes the group and writes invalid and disabled on each box.

The change between unchecked, checked and indeterminate animates the fill, the border and the opacity of the mark on motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing. Width, height and position never animate. Under reduced motion it takes motion/hover-duration.
domain_errors: invalid: the choice needs a correction, such as terms that must be accepted. The piece shows the border; the sentence is written outside it, by the page or by nph-field.
ai_hints: Use nph-checkbox when the person can check more than one option, each independent, or turns one option on or off in a form.
When the options exclude each other, use nph-radio; do not mix both in the same group.
For a group of boxes, put them in nph-field, which names the group and carries the error message; a single box does not need nph-field.
Give each box its own text; use the box alone only where the context already names it, and then fill in label.
Set indeterminate only on the item that summarizes a group checked in part, and keep it in step from the page: the piece has no group logic.
Give name and value for the form; read the state from event.target.checked on change.
Keep links, such as the terms of use, outside the piece, next to it or above it.

accessibility.semantics: A native input of type checkbox inside the component, in a label with the box and the text: role checkbox, with the state unchecked, checked or mixed. aria-invalid on the inner checkbox when invalid and not disabled.
accessibility.accessible_name: The visible text. The box alone, the label, mandatory, as the aria-label of the inner checkbox; the box and the marks are aria-hidden. Known limit: a label element outside, pointing to the host, does not name the inner checkbox, because an id does not cross the shadow root; the piece brings its own text.
keyboard: Tab enters and leaves the piece.
Enter does nothing, as on the native checkbox.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only: the box border turns focus/border and a band of focus/ring-width in focus/halo fills the 24 by 24 touch area, with the radius focus/radius-inner; with error, the border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error. Focus wins over hover; error wins over focus. Known limits, measured in the test: focus/border is below 3:1 against the halo in light `sistemas` (2.92:1), as design.md records; status/error is below 3:1 against focus/halo-error in dark, in every brand (1.96:1).
accessibility.contrast: The rule is 3:1 for the box border against the background (WCAG 1.4.11), 3:1 for the mark on the checked fill and 4.5:1 for the text; the test measures the seven brands in both schemes. The box border, color/input, measures 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark. The mark, color/primary-foreground on color/primary, is at least 4.96:1. The error border, status/error, measures 6.88:1 in light and 5.01:1 in dark. Known limit: the checked fill, color/primary, is below 3:1 against the background in dark gerencial (2.71:1) and dark rh (2.88:1); the box border, which meets 3:1, keeps the box visible.
accessibility.color_alternative: Checked and indeterminate show a mark, check or minus. The invalid piece changes its border and takes aria-invalid; the error sentence is written outside it.

invalid_combinations: disabled with invalid — disabled wins, and the error border is not drawn.
The box alone without label — the piece has no accessible name and draws nothing.
No text and no label — the piece has no accessible name and draws nothing.

parents: nph-field, which names a group of boxes

anti_patterns: Using the piece when the options exclude each other, where nph-radio is the choice.
Putting an nph-field around a single box only to give it a name.
Mixing checkbox and radio in the same group.
Putting a link or rich content in the text.
Putting the error sentence inside the piece.
Using indeterminate as an answer from the person.
Painting the box or the mark by hand.
